title: The thing with feathers
hook: hope is the thing with feathers that perches in the soul
tomorrow: who comes in a carriage to take Dickinson for a ride?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the visitor: Whitman in the war hospitals, with paper, fruit and his own presence. That closes six days of Whitman. Today, a new poet and a very small creature.

Some people tape a line to the bathroom mirror, words to get through the week. Emily Dickinson, writing in her family's house in Amherst, gave hope a body instead. ""Hope" is the thing with feathers That perches in the soul." Not a plan. Not a mood. A bird, small, landed inside, singing.
screen: `A LINE ON THE MIRROR.` → `HOPE GETS A BODY.` → `A BIRD IN THE SOUL.`

segments.voice: Look at what the bird does. It "sings the tune without the words, And never stops at all." No words: it can't argue anyone out of anything. It just keeps singing. Dickinson says it sounds sweetest in the gale, and she's heard it in the chillest land and on the strangest sea. Then the last turn: never, even at the worst, did it ask a crumb of her. That's the teaching. In Dickinson, hope isn't something you manufacture or earn. You don't even feed it. It perches on its own and asks nothing. Your part is to notice it's still singing. Now, a look back, because it's review day. Six days of Whitman. I celebrate myself, where every atom is shared. What is the grass, and an honest I don't know. I contain multitudes. In perfect silence, under the stars. Lilac and star and bird, grief with something to hold. And the visitor at the bedside. Whitman sang out loud, for everybody, in the street. Dickinson sings small, in a quiet room. Both, it turns out, listen for birds.
screen: `IT SINGS WITHOUT THE WORDS.` · `IT NEVER ASKED A CRUMB.` · `SIX DAYS OF WHITMAN.` · `TWO POETS, BOTH LISTENING FOR BIRDS.` · then, large: `THE THING WITH FEATHERS.`

segments.voice: Sit, and listen for the smallest steady sound near you: a bird outside, the fridge, your own breath. Don't decide what it means. Just let it keep going, the way Dickinson's bird never stops at all.
The thing with feathers: Dickinson's name for hope, a small bird that perches in the soul, sings without words and never asks a crumb.
For the road: the thing with feathers. It asks nothing of you; it perches, and it sings. Till next time.

howItsDone: Some readers of Dickinson learn this short poem by heart and say its first lines on hard days; some keep a small bird, a feather or a picture of one as a reminder.
